**Your dog‑walking site will be an **Amber** app** – it has logins (you’ll have a small client list), personal info (client addresses, pet details), and paid services (booking fees or subscription).  
Below is the plan we’ll follow. I’ll give you one‑screen plan plus the safety parts I’ll add automatically. After you approve, we’ll jump to Step 1 – create a safe, hosted site with form, calendar and payment.

---

## One‑screen plan

```
What we are building: A simple website for a dog‑walking business
Who uses it: You (the owner) and your clients (about 20‑50 people)
Risk level: Amber (logins, personal data, paid bookings) – we’ll add safety notes
Day‑one features: 
   1. Home page – services, about, contact form
   2. Client dashboard – secure login, view and book walks
   3. Calendar – see availability, confirm bookings
Information it stores: client names, emails, addresses, dog details, booking dates (private)
Logins: email‑only magic link (Clerk or Supabase Auth)
Money: Stripe Checkout for booking fees, no subscriptions in v1
Built with: Vite + React + Supabase + Stripe + Clerk (free tiers enough for 1‑year)
Steps:
   1. Set up Vite‑React project
   2. Add Clerk for user sign‑in + Supabase for data
   3. Build home page + landing information
   4. Create “Book a walk” form (client login required)
   5. Add Stripe Checkout button for payment
   6. Show booked walks on a local calendar
Safety:
   • Keys (Clerk, Supabase, Stripe) in .env (never in code)
   • RLS on Supabase tables (clients only see own rows)
   • Stripe webhooks verified on server
   • Logins via proven service
   • Save point before every change
   • Two‑strike rule if a step fails ×2
Not in version 1: 
   • Advanced reporting
   • Google Maps route planner
   • SMS reminders
```

**Does this look right? Reply “yes” or tell me what to change.**  
Once you say “yes”, I’ll give you the exact file changes for Step 1: creating the Vite‑React project and adding the basic folder structure.
